title: Titanium Cookware Regulatory + IP Research (Nuotao Outdoor)
product: Titanium outdoor cookware (pot/pan/lid, handle, folding, nesting)

method.policy: Official-source-first. All conclusions cite direct official fetches where possible. Dynamic/JS sites (FDA.gov, USITC HTS UI, EUR-Lex async, ECHA WAF, OEHHA list, ACCC/ProductSafety Akamai, USPTO/EUIPO trademark search) could NOT be reliably retrieved; those items are flagged evidence C and must be verified before use.

evidence_scale.A: Primary legal text retrieved directly from official source
evidence_scale.B: Official regulator page / database retrieved (guidance, searchable database output)
evidence_scale.C: Known regulatory fact, NOT directly retrieved this session (blocked/JS/queue) - verify before relying

key_warnings.no_fda_approved: FDA does NOT 'approve' cookware. 'FDA Approved' / 'FDA approved food grade' are unsupported, misleading marketing claims (FTC Act s.5 deception risk). Titanium metal is a food-contact substance (FCS); it is cleared via FCN/GRAS/prior-sanction channels, not a blanket approval label. Use 'meets FDA food-contact requirements' at most, with evidence.
key_warnings.no_ce_for_fcm: EU Food Contact Materials do NOT carry CE marking. CE is only for regulated product categories (toys, machinery, PPE...). Placing CE on cookware/FCM is misleading (1935/2004 Art.3(2) prohibits misleading labelling/presentation).
key_warnings.no_food_grade_cert: 'Food Grade' is not an official regulated certification for cookware in US/EU/CA/AU; it is a marketing descriptor. Compliance is via migration/constituent limits, not a certification stamp.
key_warnings.regulatory_not_legal_advice: This is regulatory research, NOT legal advice. Engage counsel before placing product or making claims.
key_warnings.fto_incomplete: Preliminary public patent search ≠ full Freedom-to-Operate opinion. Family status of specific CN patents shows some NOT_ACTIVE; no design/utility claim analysis done. Commission a licensed patent agent for FTO.

food_contact.regime: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) food-additive framework; food-contact substances regulated under 21 CFR 174-178; Food Contact Notification (FCN) program for new FCS.
food_contact.key_regulation: 21 CFR Part 177 'Indirect Food Additives: Polymers' (retrieved via eCFR). Note: titanium is a METAL, NOT a polymer - titanium is NOT listed in 21 CFR 177. Coatings on metal: 21 CFR 175.300.
food_contact.titanium_status: Titanium metal / CP-Ti / Ti-6Al-4V: cleared for food contact through FDA food-contact channels (FCN/GRAS/prior sanction), historically via FCNs. No blanket 'FDA approved' cookware status. FDA.gov FCN database could NOT be fetched (HTTP 401 automated-request block); confirm the specific FCN/clearance basis for your exact alloy/coating.
food_contact.evidence: A (21 CFR 177 text via eCFR); C (FCN database / alloy-specific clearance - unverified)

cpsc.note: CPSC (Consumer Product Safety Act) governs general consumer-product hazards; cookware food-contact safety sits with FDA, not CPSC. CPSC cookware guide page returned 404. Lead-in-paint (16 CFR 1303) and lead limits apply if painted/coated (relevant to non-stick/colored coatings).

ftc.note: FTC Act s.5: deceptive/unfair marketing - 'FDA Approved', 'CE', 'Food Grade' claims must be substantiated and accurate.

california_prop65.note: Proposition 65 (OEHHA): titanium metal and titanium dioxide are NOT Prop 65 listed chemicals. Relevant listed chemicals for cookware = lead/cadmium (and other heavy metals) if present in coatings/materials, which would trigger clear-and-reasonable warning. OEHHA list page is JS-rendered (could NOT extract directly); verify chemical list and safe-harbor levels before labeling.

import_tariff.hts: HTS Chapter 81, heading 8108 'Titanium and articles thereof' (e.g., 8108.90.xx 'other articles'). Exact 8-digit MFN rate + Section 301 (China origin) + country-of-origin marking (19 CFR 134) require a binding ruling / customs-broker confirmation.
import_tariff.evidence: C (USITC HTS API/UI could not be retrieved; reststop returned 503/400, view page JS)

import_labeling.note: Country-of-origin marking required on imported articles (19 CFR 134). No FDA pre-market approval for cookware. If any FDA-regulated claim (e.g., 'food grade', antimicrobial) is made, it must be truthful.

food_contact.framework: Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004 - framework for materials/articles intended to come into contact with food. Text retrieved (Art.1 scope; Art.3 general requirement: no transfer endangering health / unacceptable composition change / organoleptic deterioration; Art.3(2) no misleading labelling/advertising; Art.5 specific measures).
food_contact.specific_measure_for_metal: No EU-wide specific measure for metals (only plastic EU 10/2011, ceramics EU 84/500, etc.). Metals like titanium are regulated by national provisions (e.g., Italian/French/German national FCM rules) pending an EU metal measure.
food_contact.gmp: Commission Regulation (EC) No 2023/2006 - Good Manufacturing Practice for FCM. Full text retrieved: quality assurance system (Art.5), quality control (Art.6), documentation (Art.7), printing-ink rules (Annex A).
food_contact.evidence: A (1935/2004 and 2023/2006 via legislation.gov.uk /eur/ mirrors of EU text)

gpsr.regulation: General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 - replaces GPSD 2001/95; applies from 13 Dec 2024. Requires safe products, EU 'responsible economic operator', traceability, safety assessment, risk-based labelling/warnings.
gpsr.evidence: C (EUR-Lex returned HTTP 202 async queue; text NOT retrieved this session - verify)

reach_tio2.note: REACH Annex XVII (entry added by Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/727): restriction on titanium dioxide classified as carcinogen cat. 2 in mixtures supplied to general public (certain powder/coating forms), effective 1 Aug 2024. For SOLID titanium metal cookware body this restriction does NOT apply; it only matters if a TiO2-containing coating is supplied in restricted mixture/powder form. ECHA page blocked (403 WAF).

ce_marking.note: CE marking does NOT apply to food-contact materials/cookware. Using CE here is misleading (1935/2004 Art.3(2)).
ce_marking.evidence: C (regulatory knowledge; consistent with retrieved Art.3(2) text)

import_tariff.taric: EU Common Customs Tariff (TARIC), Chapter 81 (8108 titanium articles). Confirm exact CN code + MFN duty via TARIC.

declaration_of_compliance.note: For FCM, a 'Declaration of Compliance' (DoC) and supporting documentation (per 1935/2004 Art.15 + 2023/2006 Art.7) are expected for regulated materials; for metals, national rules apply. Keep GMP records, traceability (Art.17), and food-safety documentation.
declaration_of_compliance.evidence: A/B (framework retrieved; DoC requirement is Art.15-17, partially confirmed)

food_contact.framework: Retained (assimilated) Regulation (EC) 1935/2004 as it applies in GB (amended by The Materials and Articles in Contact with Food (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, SI 2019/704, and later). Text retrieved via legislation.gov.uk. Northern Ireland: EU rules continue under the Windsor Framework (SI 2023/959).
food_contact.gmp: Retained Commission Regulation (EC) No 2023/2006 (GMP) - text retrieved via legislation.gov.uk.
food_contact.national_rules: GB also has national food-contact rules (e.g., Materials and Articles in Contact with Food (England) Regulations 2012, SI 2012/2619) - NOT retrieved this session.

product_safety.regime: General Product Safety Regulations 2005 (SI 2005/1803) apply to Great Britain (general safety requirement, producer/distributor duties, recall). GPSR (EU) 2023/988 does NOT apply to GB (it is EU/NI law). Text retrieved: reg.5 general safety requirement, reg.6 presumption of conformity, reg.7-9 duties, Part 3 enforcement/notices.

import_tariff.uk_global_tariff: UK Global Tariff, Chapter 81 (8108 titanium articles). Confirm MFN duty + origin.

labelling.note: UKCA/CE: cookware/FCM are NOT CE-marked products; no UKCA required for FCM. Product-safety information and UK responsible person obligations apply.

food_contact.framework: Food and Drugs Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. F-27) - text retrieved. Food contact materials/packaging fall under the Act + Food and Drug Regulations.
food_contact.key_regulation: Food and Drug Regulations (C.R.C., c. 870), Division 23 'Food Packaging Materials' - retrieved: B.23.001 'No person shall sell any food in a package that may yield to its contents any substance that may be injurious to the health of a consumer of the food.' This is the general prohibition governing food-contact materials (incl. cookware contact surfaces).
food_contact.health_canada: Health Canada publishes food-contact material guidance/clearances; Health Canada FCM page returned 404 this session - verify the specific Health Canada guidance/listing for your material.
food_contact.evidence: A (FDA F-27 + FDR B.23.001); C (Health Canada guidance - unverified)

consumer_product_safety.note: Canada Consumer Product Safety Act (CCPSA, S.C. 2010, c.1) governs general consumer product hazards; cookware safety/hazards fall under CCPSA + FDR Division 23 for food contact. CCPSA page not retrieved (network error) - verify.

import_tariff.cbsa: CBSA tariff, Chapter 81 (8108 titanium articles). MFN rate + origin; confirm via CBSA.

labelling.note: Consumer Packaging and Labelling Act + Food and Drugs Act labelling apply to prepackaged food; cookware itself is subject to general consumer-product labelling/origin rules.

food_contact.regime: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (FSANZ) + State/Territory Food Acts. No EU-style positive list for food-contact materials; materials must not transfer harmful substances. FSANZ 'Chemicals in food packaging' and 'Food packaging' pages confirmed to exist (nav retrieved; body JS/truncated).
food_contact.titanium_dioxide: FSANZ has a dedicated 'Review of titanium dioxide as a food additive' page (retrieved nav confirms) - relevant to TiO2 as a food additive, NOT to titanium metal cookware; note for coatings.
food_contact.evidence: B (FSANZ pages reachable/confirmed); C (specific food-contact obligations - verify)

consumer_safety.note: ACCC product safety: cookware is NOT subject to a specific mandatory safety standard; general Australian Consumer Law (ACL) safety/consumer guarantees apply. ACCC/ProductSafety.gov.au returned 403 (Akamai) - verify mandatory-standard list.

import_tariff.abf: Australian Border Force tariff, Chapter 81 (8108 titanium articles). MFN duty + origin; confirm via ABF.

labelling.note: Country-of-origin labelling (under ACL / Commerce (Trade Descriptions) Act for goods) - confirm applicability to cookware. No mandatory 'food grade' certification.

patents.risk_summary: High filing density in CPC A47J cookware + coatings (C23C/C09D) among Chinese cookware majors and Seb/All-Clad. Folding/nesting/handle/combination and coating patents are actively claimed. Feature-level claim mapping + design patent (incl. EU Community design) screening is REQUIRED before launch. Some CN utility/design patents by titanium-specific players (苏州鑫精艺) show NOT_ACTIVE status (favorable signal) but this is preliminary.

design_patents.note: Design patents/registered designs are a major cookware risk area (e.g., EU Community designs for handles - Costa Handles EM150622220001S..009S retrieved). Full design-screen required. Evidence B (for the EU handle designs)/C (for other jurisdictions).

recommended_next_steps: Commission a licensed customs broker / tariff ruling for HTS 8108 (US/EU/UK/CA/AU) + Section 301 (China) exposure.

Obtain a Food Contact Declaration of Compliance + migration/constituent test report (e.g., per 1935/2004 + national metal rules, or FDA FCN basis) for the exact alloy, surface treatment, and any coating.
Confirm EU GPSR 2023/988 text + GB GPSR 2005 applicability, and assign EU/GB responsible persons.
Run a full FTO + design-screen (US/EU/CN/JP/KR) on handle/folding/lid/nesting/coating features via a patent attorney.
Run trademark clearance (Class 8/21/11) for the proposed brand name in target markets.
Prohibit 'FDA Approved'/'CE'/'Food Grade' claims unless legally supported; use 'meets applicable food-contact requirements' + evidence.
Check California Prop 65 for lead/cadmium in any coating and OEHHA safe-harbor limits; apply clear-and-reasonable warnings if triggered.
limitations: FDA.gov, ECHA, ACCC/ProductSafety.gov.au, EUR-Lex (async), USITC HTS, OEHHA, USPTO/EUIPO were not fully retrievable this session; corresponding items are evidence C and MUST be verified before use.
Patent search is public-database only and preliminary; no claim charts, no family expiry analysis, no design-claim mapping.
Regulatory conclusions are general and do not account for your specific alloy, finish, coating, or intended markets.
This is research, not legal advice. Confirm with qualified counsel.
